findings.title: Large simultaneous organization-review bursts intermittently return 503
findings.observed: Two 150-applicant, 150-concurrent-request runs with a five-connection pool returned 36 and 30 unexpected institutions_unavailable responses during verification. The same test passed at concurrency 30. Later instrumented 150-concurrency runs also passed, so the failure is timing/load-sensitive rather than deterministic.
findings.measuredCost: The isolated reviewer transaction probe measured 113 SQL queries per verification when rebuilding a 100-item submission queue.
findings.likelyCause: Per-item queue queries run before COMMIT while the reviewer subject lock is held. Together with the five-second pool acquisition limit this creates avoidable queueing pressure. The failed runs did not capture the underlying pool exception, so pool exhaustion remains a strongly supported explanation, not a directly captured exception.
findings.suggestedFix: Bulk-fetch review-queue representatives and parent details, shorten the mutation transaction, and bound reviewer request concurrency. Preserve authorization checks and retest dropped responses before adding retries.
findings.state: Identified; not fixed in this testing task
